assertion.rationale: F1: data-api has ingressExternal:true and zero inbound authentication (app.ts:56) — anyone who finds the FQDN reads Defender posture, Dependabot alerts and Log Analytics results, and can loop full table scans. F1 is NOT closed; it is Task 6, pending. F2: the MCP auth gate was inert in the shipped configuration — it threw only in backendMode 'cloud', MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is set nowhere in infra/ or .github/, so /healthz reported auth.enforced:false to anyone. F2 is now CLOSED (Tasks 4 and 5). Task 4 closed the application half: loadInboundAuth (auth-gate.ts) no longer conditions enforcement on backendMode, so local mode — the configuration that actually ships — now fails closed at boot without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN or an explicit MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED opt-out, and the gate is mounted ahead of the body parser. Task 5 closed the infra half: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep no longer declares a `@secure()` mcpAuthToken parameter (deleted, along with demo.bicepparam's empty default); the mcp-tools container app instead resolves the mcp-auth-token secret directly from the platform Key Vault at runtime via a keyVaultUrl + identity reference, using a Key Vault Secrets User grant on the mcp-tools UAMI (module mcpKvGrant, reusing modules/key-vault-secrets-user-role.bicep, previously unreferenced since the 2026-08-24 Anthropic removal). The token therefore never enters this template, demo.bicepparam, ARM deployment history or a what-if log, and no workflow reads or exports it. MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is now set explicitly via the mcpToolsBackendMode parameter (default 'local') instead of being absent from every workflow. F3: the Direct Line token endpoint mints tokens to unauthenticated callers whenever DIRECTLINE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset or Origin is absent, and that path carries the MCP token, making F2's now-closed gate irrelevant to it — F3 is a separate, still-open exposure. F3 is NOT closed; it is Task 7, pending. F13: zero workload RBAC is expressed anywhere in IaC — the only role assignments in the estate are deployer-to-Owner and verifier-to-Reader, both at subscription scope in PowerShell; seven documented workload grants (data-api, mcp-tools, cost-ingest) exist nowhere as code, so access is not limited to authorized users, processes or devices by construction. Task 5's mcpKvGrant module is one workload RBAC grant now expressed in IaC, but it does not close F13: the other six documented grants (SQL contained-database users, Fabric workspace roles, Cost Management Reader, Log Analytics/Security Reader) are still made only by out-of-band scripts, not IaC. F13 is NOT closed; it is Task 12, pending. Overall status stays GAP: F1 and F13 remain open, and F3 (which independently exposes the MCP token regardless of F2's status) remains open too.

recommendation: Set ingressExternal:false on data-api (both frontends already proxy /api/ server-side). Make the Direct Line endpoint refuse (500) when DIRECTLINE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset and refuse (403) when Origin is absent. Express the remaining six documented workload RBAC grants (data-api, mcp-tools, cost-ingest) in IaC and add a criterion asserting each principal holds exactly its expected roles. (The MCP auth gate default and Key Vault token resolution recommended here previously are DONE — Tasks 4 and 5.)
